reviewer.role: SME and architect (GitHub Copilot, acting on the user's instruction)

elements.note: The interest formula is a pure policy class, testable without files.
Only streamAll() is used; findByAccountId is not needed by any rule.
update takes an Account.Change: only the balances the operation assigned are rewritten, over the stored image (see X-01).
findDefaultByGroupId became a second find with the DEFAULT group id (rateFor).
AccountStatus is kept as the stored text: no rule in this program reads it.

rules.note: The record count is never displayed or written by the program, so it has no normalized counterpart.
The balance (ADD) and both cycle totals (MOVE 0) are rewritten; the credit limits keep their stored bytes.

quirks.note: The unreachable end-of-file branch is not carried over; removing dead code changes nothing. Because that branch never runs, the last account's cycle is never closed (see F-01). The implementation reproduces this consequence.
A missing account abends the step before the stale record could be used.
A missing cross-reference abends the step.
A missing group rate falls back to DEFAULT; a missing DEFAULT abends.
The transaction id is the 10-character PARM prefix followed by a 6-digit sequence; a short PARM is space-padded, as the STRING statement leaves it.
Unused description bytes hold the storage default (x'00' in the oracle), not spaces.

deviations.what: computeInterest became InterestPolicy; updateAccount became Account.closeCycleWithInterest.

implementationDefects.symptom: ACCTDATA differed from the faithful program when positive amounts were stored with an unsigned zone (F-sign).
implementationDefects.cause: The account rewrite re-encoded every numeric field, so unsigned-zone credit limits came back with a signed zone. COBOL REWRITE changes only the fields the program assigned.
implementationDefects.fix: Account.closeCycleWithInterest returns an Account.Change assigning the balance and both cycle totals; RecordLayouts.account(Change, stored) writes exactly those and keeps every other stored byte.
implementationDefects.guardNote: Re-verified 2026-10-06 by mutation: re-encoding every field, or writing only fields whose value changed, both fail 'positive numbers stored unsigned (F-sign)'.

smeFindings.finding: Interest for the last account in the category-balance file is written as transactions, but that account's balance is never increased and its cycle credit/debit are never reset. Every run under-posts one account.
smeFindings.evidence: Scenario 'one account only (Q-01)': SYSTRAN has the interest transactions while ACCTDATA is unchanged; the GnuCOBOL oracle behaves the same for the last account of the CardDemo month (normalizedEqualsGnuCobolOracle matches it byte for byte).
smeFindings.recommendation: Keep for parity until the business confirms the defect. The fix is one call after the loop (close the last account's cycle); it would make the normalized implementation differ from the oracle on purpose, so it needs a new approved requirement and a new requirementsHash.
